p.src: Now Song Jiang spoke to the assembled heroes at the feast: “Since you rescued this humble Song Jiang and brought me up the mountain, I have spent day after day feasting here and have been exceedingly happy. Yet I do not know how my aged father is faring at home. At present Jiangzhou will surely report the matter to the capital, which will then send orders to Jizhou instructing Yuncheng County to arrest my family and hold them until the principal offender is caught. I fear my aged father’s life may not be spared. I cannot cease thinking of him, and wish to go home and bring my aged father up the mountain, so that I may be free of this anxiety. I do not know whether my brothers will permit it.” Chao Gai said, “Worthy brother, this is a matter of the highest human duty. How could we enjoy ourselves here while letting your aged father suffer at home? Of course we shall grant your wish. It is only that our brothers have endured much hardship these past days and the troops in the stronghold are not yet settled. Wait another two days; then we shall muster the men of the stronghold and go straight there to bring him back.” Song Jiang said, “Elder brother, ordinarily a few more days would make no difference, but I fear Jiangzhou’s orders may reach Jizhou and they will arrest my family. That is why the matter must not be delayed. There is no need to send many men now. I shall go secretly by myself and, together with my brother Song Qing, bring our aged father up the mountain by night. Then no one in the countryside will know a thing. If I take many companions, it will surely alarm the villagers and instead cause inconvenience.” Chao Gai said, “Worthy brother, if some mishap befalls you on the road, there will be no one to save you.” Song Jiang said, “If it is for my father’s sake, I shall bear no resentment even if I die.” That day, no matter how earnestly they tried, they could not persuade him to stay. Song Jiang insisted on leaving, so he put on a felt hat, took up a short staff, fastened a sharp blade at his waist, and descended the mountain. The chieftains escorted him beyond Golden Sands Strand, then returned.

p.src: Now Song Jiang crossed the water and went ashore at Zhu Gui’s tavern, then took the highway toward Yuncheng County. Along the way, as was inevitable, he ate when hungry, drank when thirsty, lodged by night, and traveled at dawn. One day, while hurrying toward Song Family Village, night overtook him before he could arrive, so he lodged at an inn. The next day he hastened on and reached Song Family Village while it was still early. He hid in the woods until evening, then went to the manor and knocked at the rear gate. Someone inside heard the knock, and presently Song Qing came out to open the gate. At the sight of his elder brother, he was greatly startled. In alarm he said, “Elder brother, why have you come home?” Song Jiang said, “I came especially to fetch Father and you.” Song Qing said, “Elder brother, everyone here now knows what you did in Jiangzhou. The county has assigned the two constables Zhao to come and summon us every day. They keep us under close watch, and we cannot stir. They are only waiting for the official documents from Jiangzhou. Once those arrive, they will seize Father and me, throw us into prison, and keep us there until you are caught. Day and night, one or two hundred local soldiers patrol the area. You must not delay. Hurry back to Liangshan Marsh and ask the chieftains to come down and rescue Father and your brother.”

p.src: When Song Jiang heard this, his whole body broke out in a cold sweat. Not daring to enter the gate, he turned and fled, taking the road back toward Liangshan Marsh. That night the moonlight was dim and the road indistinct. Song Jiang thought only of choosing lonely side paths as he went. He had walked for about one watch when he suddenly heard men raising a hue and cry behind him. Song Jiang turned his head and listened. Only a mile or two away, he saw a cluster of torches blazing brightly and heard men shout, “Song Jiang, stop!” As Song Jiang ran, he thought to himself, “I did not heed Chao Gai’s words, and now this calamity has indeed befallen me. Merciful Heaven, take pity and save Song Jiang!” He saw a place in the distance and ran toward it without another thought. Presently the wind swept aside the thin clouds and revealed the bright moon. Only then did Song Jiang clearly recognize the place; he cried out in dismay, scarcely knowing what to do. The place before him was known as Return-to-the-Road Village. It was completely encircled by steep mountains and lofty ridges, with a stream running all around their foot, and only a single road through the middle. Once inside the village, whichever way one turned, there was only this same road and no other. p.src: The enclosing walls were crumbling, the halls leaning askew; Green moss spread across the painted walls of both galleries, and emerald grass sprouted between the patterned bricks covering the ground. Before the gate, a little demon had lost an arm and no longer looked fearsome; In the hall, the judge lacked his official cap and so had lost all proper dignity. Spiders spun webs across the offering table, while mole crickets and ants built nests inside the incense burner; Foxes often slept inside the paper-burning furnace, and bats never left the divine canopy.

p.src: Song Jiang had no choice but to push open the temple gate. By the moonlight he entered and searched for a place to hide. He examined the front and rear halls for a while but found nowhere to conceal himself, and his panic only grew. Then he heard someone outside say, “Surely he can only have run into this temple?” When Song Jiang heard it, he recognized Zhao Neng’s voice. With no time and nowhere to hide, he saw a shrine cabinet in the hall. Song Jiang lifted the curtain, thrust himself inside, and crawled into the cabinet. He laid down his short staff, curled himself into a heap inside, and did not dare even breathe. He heard men outside carrying torches and shining their light into the temple.

p.src: Peering secretly from the shrine cabinet, Song Jiang saw Zhao Neng and Zhao De leading forty or fifty men. Each carried a torch and shone it into every corner, drawing ever closer to the hall. Song Jiang prayed, “This time I have run into a dead end. Spirits of the dead, shelter me; divine powers, protect me!” One after another they all passed by, but no one looked inside the shrine cabinet. Song Jiang thought, “Is this not a stroke of heavenly fortune?” But then Zhao De brought his torch over to shine inside the cabinet. Song Jiang thought, “This time I shall truly be bound and taken.” Holding his sword-staff in one hand, Zhao De lifted the divine curtain with its shaft and swept the torchlight up and down. The flame sent a cloud of smoke surging upward, dislodging a shower of black dust that fell squarely into Zhao De’s eyes. Blinded by it, he dropped the torch to the ground and stamped it out. He walked out of the hall and said to the local soldiers, “That scoundrel is not in the temple. But there is no other road—where could he have gone?” The soldiers said, “Most likely the scoundrel ran into the woods inside the village. There is no fear of his escaping from here. This village is called Return-to-the-Road Village, and it has only this one road in and out. Though there are high mountains and woods inside, there is no path leading up through them. Constable, you need only hold the village entrance. Even if he could sprout wings and fly to heaven, he would not escape. At daybreak we shall search the village thoroughly and seize him.” Zhao De said, “That is true.” He led the soldiers down from the hall.

p.src: The men came back into the temple to search again. Song Jiang said, “My fate is so cruelly thwarted that this time I am surely finished.” They searched everywhere, before and behind the hall, but never thought to turn over the bricks. After they had searched once more, their torches gradually cast their light up into the hall. Zhao Neng said, “Most likely he is hiding in the shrine cabinet. My brother did not look closely enough just now. I shall shine a light in there myself.” A local soldier held up a torch while Zhao Neng raised the curtain with one hand, and five or seven men craned their heads forward to look. Had they not looked, nothing would have happened; but the moment they did, a vicious gust suddenly whirled out of the shrine cabinet and extinguished every torch. Pitch darkness enveloped the temple, and no one could see the person before him. Zhao Neng said, “There is something uncanny here again. For such a violent wind to rise from level ground—the deity must be within, and surely resents our continually shining lights upon him. He has raised this gale to manifest his displeasure. Let us leave for now. We need only guard the village entrance and return to seek him at daybreak.” Zhao De said, “But we still have not examined the shrine cabinet carefully. Let us thrust a spear into it a few times.” “That is true,” said Zhao Neng.

p.src: Just as the two were about to advance, another uncanny gale rose behind the hall. It sent sand flying and stones tumbling down, shook the whole building with a rattling tremor, and drew a black cloud over heaven and earth. An invading chill made every hair stand on end. Zhao Neng knew that all was not well and called to Zhao De, “Run, brother! The deity is displeased.” With a great clamor, they all rushed down from the hall and fled toward the temple gate. Some tumbled headlong and others sprained their legs, but they scrambled up again and ran for their lives out of the temple. Then cries came from within the temple: “Have mercy on us!” When Zhao Neng went back in to look, he found two or three local soldiers fallen in the forecourt, their clothes caught on tree roots. They could not wrench themselves free for the life of them; having dropped their sabers, they tugged at their garments and cried for mercy. Hearing this from inside the shrine cabinet, Song Jiang could not help laughing.

p.src: Song Jiang then asked, “From whence have you two immortal attendants come?” The attendants in blue replied, “By command of Her Ladyship, we have come to invite the Star-Lord to her palace.” Song Jiang said, “You immortal attendants are mistaken. My surname is Song and my given name is Jiang. I am no Star-Lord.” The attendants in blue said, “How could we be mistaken? Please come at once, Star-Lord. Her Ladyship has long been waiting.” Song Jiang asked, “What lady is this? I have never had the honor of meeting her. How could I dare go?” The attendants in blue replied, “You will know when you arrive, Star-Lord. There is no need to inquire.” Song Jiang asked, “Where is Her Ladyship?” The attendants in blue replied, “In the palace just behind here.” The attendants in blue went ahead to lead the way. Song Jiang followed them down from the hall and around the rear hall to a small corner gate in a side wall. One attendant said, “Star-Lord Song, enter here.” Song Jiang followed them through the corner gate and saw a sky filled with stars and moonlight, fragrant breezes blowing gently, and flourishing woods and tall bamboos on every side. Song Jiang thought, “So there is such a place behind this temple. Had I known, I would have hidden here and been spared all those terrors.” As Song Jiang walked on, he saw two rows of great pines planted along the fragrant path, each so broad that two men could scarcely encircle it. Between them ran a broad, level avenue paved in a tortoiseshell pattern. Looking upon it, Song Jiang mused, “I would never have imagined that such a fine road lay behind this ancient temple.” He followed the attendants in blue for less than a li before hearing the murmuring sound of a mountain stream. Looking ahead, he saw a bridge of green stone with vermilion railings on both sides. Along the banks grew rare flowers, exotic grasses, ancient pines, luxuriant bamboos, green willows, and blossoming peach trees. Beneath the bridge, water churned like rolling snow and tumbling silver before flowing away through a cavern in the rock. After crossing the bridge and looking ahead, he saw two rows of wondrous trees, with a great vermilion Lingxing Gate between them. When Song Jiang passed through the Lingxing Gate, he raised his eyes and beheld a palace. This is what he saw:

Coiling dragons wound round the pillars and played with shining pearls; paired phoenixes upon the curtains and screens gleamed in the morning sun. Beyond walls of red clay, imperial willows mingled profusely with palace flowers; Around towers and terraces wreathed in emerald mist, a pale auspicious radiance enveloped blessed forms. p.src: Song Jiang scrambled to his feet and looked around. The moon stood at its zenith, so he reckoned it was about the third watch. When he felt inside his sleeves, he found three date stones in his hand and the Heavenly Books wrapped in a kerchief within his sleeve. He took them out and looked. They truly were the three volumes of the Heavenly Books, and he could still taste the fragrance of wine in his mouth. Song Jiang thought, “This dream was extraordinary indeed—a dream, yet not a dream. If it was only a dream, how can these Heavenly Books be in my sleeve, the fragrance of wine remain in my mouth, and the date stones lie in my hand? And why do I remember every word she spoke to me without forgetting a single sentence? Yet if it was not a dream, I plainly remember being in the divine kitchen and falling headlong into it. What is so difficult to understand about that? This sacred being of the place must be supremely efficacious, and thus manifested herself to me. But I do not know what deity she is.” He raised the shrine curtain and looked. Seated upon the nine-dragon chair was a goddess of wondrous countenance, exactly as she had appeared in his dream. Song Jiang thought, “This goddess called me Star Lord. It seems I was no ordinary being in my former life. These three volumes of the Heavenly Books must surely serve some purpose. Nor have I forgotten the four lines of heavenly revelation she entrusted to me. The blue-robed maiden said, ‘At daybreak, you will naturally escape the peril of this village.’ Now the sky is gradually brightening, so I shall go out.”

Chieftain Chao still could not set his mind at rest, so he ordered all of us to come and support you, fearing that some mishap might befall you. p.src: Now the whole company of men and horses left Huandao Village and returned directly to Liangshan Marsh. Scholar Wu led the chieftains who had remained to guard the mountain as far as Golden Sands Beach to welcome them. They all proceeded to the Hall of Righteous Assembly in the great stronghold, where the valiant men greeted one another. Song Jiang urgently asked, “Where is my father?” Chao Gai at once ordered that the venerable Lord Song be invited forth. Before long, Song Qing, the Iron Fan, came guiding a mountain sedan chair in which the venerable lord was carried. The others helped him out of the chair and supported him into the hall. At the sight of him, Song Jiang felt joy descend from heaven, and his face broke into a radiant smile. He bowed twice and said, “My honored father has suffered great fear. I, Song Jiang, have proved an unfilial son and caused you to endure such fright and distress.” The venerable Lord Song said, “Those intolerable scoundrels Zhao Neng and his brother posted men to keep constant watch over us every day. They were only waiting for the official warrant from Jiangzhou, whereupon they meant to seize both father and son and deliver us to the authorities. When we heard you knocking at the rear gate of the manor, eight or nine local soldiers were already in the thatched hall out front. Later they vanished; I do not know how they came to rush outside! At the third watch, more than two hundred men opened the manor gate, helped me into a sedan chair, and carried me away. They told your brother Silang to pack the trunks and then set fire to the manor. At the time I was given no chance to ask the reason and was brought straight here.” Song Jiang said, “That father and son are reunited today is entirely thanks to the efforts of all my brothers.” He called upon his brother Song Qing to bow and thank all the chieftains. When Chao Gai and the others had all finished paying their respects to the venerable Lord Song, they slaughtered oxen and horses and laid out a celebratory feast in honor of the reunion of Song Gongming and his father. That day they drank their fill before dispersing. The next day another banquet was prepared in celebration, and every chieftain, great and small, rejoiced.

p.src: On the third day, Chao Gai privately prepared another feast to celebrate the reunion of Song Jiang and his father. Suddenly, a thought stirred in Gongsun Sheng: he remembered his aged mother in Jizhou and wondered how she fared after his long absence from home. While everyone was drinking, Gongsun Sheng rose and addressed the assembled chiefs: “For so long, I have had the good fortune to enjoy the companionship of you gallant heroes, whose kindness has made us as close as flesh and blood. Yet ever since I followed Chief Chao to the mountain, I have spent each day amid feasting and merriment and have never once returned home to visit my aged mother. I also fear that my true master may be anxiously awaiting me. I wish to return home for a visit and take leave of you chiefs for three or five months, after which I shall come back to see you. Thus I may fulfill my wish and spare my aged mother further anxious longing.” Chao Gai said, “I heard you mention before that your honored mother had no one to attend her in the north. Since you have now spoken thus, it would be hard to detain you, though I cannot bear for us to part. Although you mean to leave, wait until tomorrow, and we shall see you off.” Gongsun Sheng thanked him. That day they drank until all were thoroughly intoxicated, then dispersed and retired to their rooms to rest. Early the next morning, a banquet was laid below the pass to bid Gongsun Sheng farewell.

p.src: Now Gongsun Sheng once more dressed as a wandering Daoist. He fastened his waist pouch and belly pouch about him, carried his paired precious swords on his back, hung a palm-leaf hat from his shoulder, took a tortoiseshell fan in his hand, and descended the mountain. The chiefs met him below, and at the banquet by the pass each raised a cup to bid him farewell. When all had offered their farewell cups, Chao Gai said, “Master Yiqing, since you are resolved to go, we cannot keep you, but you must not break your word. In truth, I would not permit you to leave, but as your venerable mother still lives, I dare not stand in your way. Once a hundred days have passed, we shall eagerly await your honored return. By no means fail to keep your promise.” Gongsun Sheng replied, “For so long I have received the generous regard of all you chiefs. How could I dare break my word? Once I have returned home to pay my respects to my true master and made arrangements for my aged mother, I shall come straight back to the stronghold.” Song Jiang said, “Why not take several men with you and have them bring your venerable mother up to the mountain? Then you could attend her morning and evening.” Gongsun Sheng replied, “My mother has loved peace and quiet all her life and cannot abide fright or commotion. For that reason, I dare not bring her here. Our family has its own fields and country estate, which my mother is quite able to manage herself. I shall merely go to visit her once, then return so that we may again gather here in fellowship.” Song Jiang said, “Since that is so, we shall do entirely as you wish. We ask only that you favor us with an early return!” Chao Gai brought out a tray of gold and silver for his journey, but Gongsun Sheng said, “There is no need for so much. Enough to cover my travel expenses will suffice.” Chao Gai insisted that he accept half. Gongsun Sheng tied it securely inside his waist pouch, made a Daoist bow, bade everyone farewell, crossed the Golden Sands, and set out toward Jizhou.

p.src: After the chiefs’ banquet had broken up and they were about to return up the mountain, they suddenly saw Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind, burst into loud sobs below the pass. Song Jiang hurriedly asked, “Brother, what is troubling you?” Li Kui cried, “Why the hell shouldn’t I be angry? This one goes to fetch his father, that one goes to see his mother, but Iron Ox alone must have crawled out of a hole in the earth!” Chao Gai asked, “Then what do you mean to do now?” Li Kui said, “I have only my old mother back home. My elder brother works as a hired hand in another man’s household. How can he possibly give my mother a happy life? I want to fetch her here so she may enjoy herself for a while.” Chao Gai said, “What you say is right, brother. I shall send several men with you to bring her up the mountain. That too would be an excellent thing.” Song Jiang promptly said, “That will not do. Brother Li is unruly by nature; if he returns to his native village, something is certain to go wrong. Nor would it be wise to send others with him. Besides, his temper is like raging fire, and he is bound to clash with people along the road. He also killed many people in Jiangzhou. Who would not recognize him as the Black Whirlwind? By now, how could the authorities have failed to circulate official notices there? They will surely be hunting for him in his native district. And with your fierce appearance, if some mishap befell you so far away, how would we ever learn of it? Wait a while. Once we learn that matters have quieted down, it will not be too late to go and fetch her.” Li Kui grew agitated and shouted, “Brother, you are an unfair man too! You wanted to bring your father up the mountain to live happily, yet my mother is to be left suffering in the village. Wouldn’t that make Iron Ox’s belly burst with anger!” Song Jiang said, “Brother, do not be so impatient. Since you are determined to fetch your mother, obey me in three matters, and I shall let you go.” Li Kui said, “Then tell me what those three matters are.” Song Jiang held up two fingers and declared those three conditions. And thus it came about that Li Kui would wield his earth-shaking, heaven-rocking might and battle the tiger that bounded over the hills and leapt across the ravines. But what were the three conditions Song Jiang laid down for Li Kui? Listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
